reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The test cleanup permanently deletes pre-existing `pyoaev` modules, including shared stubs, making subsequent imports order-dependent instead of restoring the original entries.
1 open issue - [Restore pre-existing SDK modules after cleanup](https://github.com/OpenAEV-Platform/injectors/pull/560#discussion_r4684025626) · New
What changed in this PR Fixes #477 by passing the inject message to NetExec’s execution-message builder, allowing asset-group injects to read group names without raising `KeyError: 'assetGroups'`. **Changes:** - Uses the inject message rather than parsed contract fields when building execution messages. - Adds a regression test checking that the callback message includes the asset-group name and selected hostname. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `netexec/​test/​test_asset_group_execution_message.py` | Adds regression coverage for asset-group execution messages. | | `netexec/​netexec/​openaev_netexec.py` | Passes the correct data source to the execution-message builder. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: This cleanup deletes pre-existing SDK modules too, including the stubs installed by `test/conftest.py`. Other test modules retain references to those objects, but subsequent SDK imports no longer receive the same modules and may load the real SDK instead, making the test environment import-order dependent. Preserve and restore the original `pyoaev` entries rather than deleting them permanently.
